events.title: The US hockey team beats the Soviet Union in the Miracle on Ice
events.summary: An Olympic upset becomes one of sport's most famous games.
events.description: On February 22, 1980, the US men's ice hockey team defeated the Soviet Union's team at the Winter Olympics in Lake Placid, New York, in the game known as the Miracle on Ice.
events.notificationBody: In 1980, the US men's hockey team stunned the Soviet Union in the Miracle on Ice.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 22
Encyclopaedia Britannica - Miracle on Ice

events.title: George Washington is born in Virginia
events.dateNote: Gregorian date. Under the Julian (Old Style) calendar then used in the British colonies, he was born on February 11, 1731.
events.summary: The future first US president is born in Westmoreland County.
events.description: On February 22, 1732, George Washington, commander of the colonial armies in the American Revolution and the first US president, was born in Westmoreland County, Virginia.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 22
Encyclopaedia Britannica - George Washington

events.title: White Rose resisters are executed in Munich
events.summary: Hans and Sophie Scholl and Christoph Probst are put to death for opposing the Nazis.
events.description: On February 22, 1943, three members of the White Rose, an anti-Nazi student group at the University of Munich, were beheaded in Munich for distributing leaflets against the regime.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - White Rose

events.title: The first Daytona 500 is run
events.summary: Lee Petty wins NASCAR's new race.
events.description: On February 22, 1959, NASCAR held the first Daytona 500, which was won by Lee Petty.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 22

events.title: An earthquake devastates Christchurch, New Zealand
events.summary: A magnitude 6.3 aftershock strikes the city.
events.description: On February 22, 2011, Christchurch, New Zealand, and its surrounding area were struck by a massively destructive magnitude 6.3 aftershock.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 22

events.title: US servicemen raise the flag on Iwo Jima
events.summary: Six men raise the American flag on Mount Suribachi.
events.description: On February 23, 1945, during World War II, six US servicemen raised the American flag over Mount Suribachi on the island of Iwo Jima.
events.notificationBody: In 1945, six US servicemen raised the American flag on Mount Suribachi, Iwo Jima.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 23

events.title: The siege of the Alamo begins
events.summary: Santa Anna's army surrounds the Texan defenders.
events.description: On February 23, 1836, during the Texas Revolution, Mexican General Antonio Lopez de Santa Anna began a siege of the Alamo, which was captured after 13 days.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 23

events.title: George Frideric Handel is born in Halle
events.summary: The composer of Messiah is born.
events.description: On February 23, 1685, the composer George Frideric Handel, a leading figure of late Baroque music, was born in Halle, Germany.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 23
Encyclopaedia Britannica - George Frideric Handel

events.title: W.E.B. Du Bois is born
events.summary: The scholar and civil rights leader is born in Massachusetts.
events.description: On February 23, 1868, W.E.B. Du Bois, one of the most important African American protest leaders of the early 20th century, was born in Great Barrington, Massachusetts.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 23
Encyclopaedia Britannica - W.E.B. Du Bois

events.title: Boston is granted a city charter
events.summary: The Massachusetts town officially becomes a city.
events.description: On February 23, 1822, Boston was granted a charter to become a city.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 23

events.title: Pope Gregory XIII decrees the Gregorian calendar
events.dateNote: Julian calendar date; the bull introduced the Gregorian calendar later that year.
events.summary: A papal bull orders ten days dropped from the year.
events.description: On February 24, 1582, Pope Gregory XIII issued a papal bull reforming the calendar: Thursday, October 4, 1582, would be followed by Friday, October 15.
events.notificationTitle: Ten days vanish from the calendar
events.notificationBody: In 1582, Pope Gregory XIII decreed that October 4 would be followed by October 15.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 24

events.title: The Supreme Court decides Marbury v. Madison
events.summary: The court strikes down an act of Congress as unconstitutional.
events.description: On February 24, 1803, in Marbury v. Madison, the US Supreme Court declared an act of Congress unconstitutional, establishing the principle of judicial review.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 24

events.title: Russia launches a full-scale invasion of Ukraine
events.summary: The largest war in Europe in decades begins.
events.description: On February 24, 2022, Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 24

events.title: The House impeaches President Andrew Johnson
events.summary: The vote is 126 to 47.
events.description: On February 24, 1868, the US House of Representatives voted 126 to 47 to impeach President Andrew Johnson.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 24

events.title: King Louis-Philippe abdicates as revolution reaches France
events.summary: The Revolutions of 1848 topple the French monarchy.
events.description: On February 24, 1848, the anti-monarchical Revolutions of 1848 reached France and led to the abdication of King Louis-Philippe.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 24

events.title: Cassius Clay defeats Sonny Liston for the heavyweight title
events.summary: The young boxer, soon to be Muhammad Ali, becomes world champion.
events.description: On February 25, 1964, Cassius Clay, later known as Muhammad Ali, defeated reigning world heavyweight champion Sonny Liston.
events.notificationTitle: The upset that made a legend
events.notificationBody: In 1964, Cassius Clay, later Muhammad Ali, beat Sonny Liston for the heavyweight title.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 25

events.title: Khrushchev denounces Stalin in a secret speech
events.summary: The Soviet leader attacks his late predecessor.
events.description: On February 25, 1956, the Twentieth Congress of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union closed after First Secretary Nikita Khrushchev delivered a secret speech denouncing the late Joseph Stalin.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 25

events.title: Hiram Revels becomes the first African American in Congress
events.summary: He is sworn in to the US Senate.
events.description: On February 25, 1870, Hiram Rhodes Revels was sworn in to the US Senate, becoming the first African American to serve in Congress.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 25

events.title: Ferdinand Marcos flees the Philippines
events.summary: The president leaves for Hawaii under US pressure.
events.description: On February 25, 1986, Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos, under pressure from the United States, fled the country for Hawaii.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 25

events.title: George Harrison is born
events.summary: The Beatles' lead guitarist is born.
events.description: On February 25, 1943, the British musician George Harrison, lead guitarist of the Beatles, was born.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 25

events.title: Napoleon escapes from exile on Elba
events.summary: The deposed emperor slips away to begin the Hundred Days.
events.description: On February 26, 1815, Napoleon, banished to the island of Elba by a coalition of European powers the year before, escaped from exile.
events.notificationTitle: An emperor slips out of exile
events.notificationBody: In 1815, Napoleon escaped from exile on the island of Elba.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 26

events.title: Victor Hugo is born in Besancon
events.summary: The author of Les Miserables is born.
events.description: On February 26, 1802, the French writer Victor Hugo, author of The Hunchback of Notre-Dame and Les Miserables, was born in Besancon, France.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Victor Hugo

events.title: Grand Teton National Park is established
events.summary: Wyoming's mountain park joins the national park system.
events.description: On February 26, 1929, Grand Teton National Park was established in Wyoming. In 1950 it was expanded to include most of Jackson Hole National Monument.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 26

events.title: Johnny Cash is born
events.summary: The 'Man in Black' of country music is born.
events.description: On February 26, 1932, the singer-songwriter Johnny Cash, known to fans as the Man in Black, was born. He broadened the scope of American country music.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 26

events.title: A truck bomb explodes beneath the World Trade Center
events.summary: The attack in New York kills six people.
events.description: On February 26, 1993, a truck bomb exploded in the garage of the World Trade Center in New York City, killing six people and injuring more than 1,000.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 26

events.title: Radar operators pick up radio waves from the Sun
events.summary: Physicist James Stanley Hey traces wartime radar jamming to the Sun.
events.description: On February 27, 1942, the British physicist James Stanley Hey noticed strange interference on British radar equipment, which he traced to radio waves from the Sun, a founding discovery of radio astronomy.
events.notificationBody: In 1942, James Stanley Hey discovered that the Sun gives off radio waves.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 27

events.title: The Reichstag building burns in Berlin
events.summary: Fire guts the home of Germany's parliament.
events.description: On February 27, 1933, the Reichstag, the building of Germany's parliament in Berlin, caught fire.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 27

events.title: A magnitude 8.8 earthquake strikes Chile
events.summary: The quake and tsunami kill more than 500 people.
events.description: On February 27, 2010, a magnitude 8.8 earthquake struck Chile, triggering a tsunami that devastated coastal areas. It was the region's most powerful earthquake since 1960 and caused more than 500 deaths.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 27

events.title: The American Indian Movement occupies Wounded Knee
events.summary: About 200 activists take over the South Dakota hamlet.
events.description: On February 27, 1973, about 200 members of the American Indian Movement occupied Wounded Knee, a hamlet on a reservation in South Dakota.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 27

events.title: John Steinbeck is born in Salinas
events.summary: The author of The Grapes of Wrath is born in California.
events.description: On February 27, 1902, the writer John Steinbeck, author of The Grapes of Wrath and winner of the 1962 Nobel Prize for Literature, was born in Salinas, California.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 27
Encyclopaedia Britannica - John Steinbeck

events.title: M*A*S*H ends with a record-setting finale
events.summary: More than 106 million viewers watch the last episode.
events.description: On February 28, 1983, more than 106 million people watched 'Goodbye, Farewell and Amen', the final episode of the television series M*A*S*H. It remains the most-watched episode of scripted television.
events.notificationBody: In 1983, more than 106 million people watched the final episode of M*A*S*H.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 28
Encyclopaedia Britannica - Today in History: M*A*S*H Series Finale

events.title: Pope Benedict XVI resigns
events.summary: He is the first pope to step down since 1415.
events.description: On February 28, 2013, Benedict XVI became the first pope to resign since Gregory XII in 1415.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 28

events.title: Egypt is declared independent
events.summary: The British protectorate over Egypt ends.
events.description: On February 28, 1922, Egypt declared its independence, ending the British protectorate.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 28

events.title: The 228 Incident spreads across Taiwan
events.summary: Protests against the ruling Kuomintang sweep the island.
events.description: On February 28, 1947, protests against the ruling Kuomintang (KMT) spread across Taiwan, in what became known as the 228 Incident.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 28

events.title: Swedish Prime Minister Olof Palme is assassinated
events.summary: The internationally prominent leader is shot in Stockholm.
events.description: On February 28, 1986, Olof Palme, the internationally prominent prime minister of Sweden, was assassinated.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 28

events.title: Hattie McDaniel becomes the first African American to win an Oscar
events.summary: She is honored for her role in Gone with the Wind.
events.description: On February 29, 1940, Hattie McDaniel became the first African American to win an Academy Award, for best supporting actress in Gone with the Wind (1939).
events.notificationTitle: A leap-day first at the Oscars
events.notificationBody: In 1940, Hattie McDaniel became the first African American to win an Academy Award.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 29

events.title: Gioachino Rossini is born in Pesaro
events.summary: The composer of The Barber of Seville is born on a leap day.
events.description: On February 29, 1792, the Italian composer Gioachino Rossini, best known for comic operas such as The Barber of Seville, was born in Pesaro.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 29
Encyclopaedia Britannica - Gioachino Rossini

events.title: Morarji Desai is born
events.summary: India's first prime minister from outside the Congress party is born.
events.description: On February 29, 1896, Morarji Desai was born. As prime minister of India (1977-79), he was the first leader of independent India not to represent the Indian National Congress party.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 29

events.title: Gordie Howe scores his 800th NHL goal
events.summary: At 51, he is the first player to reach the mark.
events.description: On February 29, 1980, at the age of 51, the Canadian hockey player Gordie Howe became the first to score 800 goals in the National Hockey League.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 29

events.title: The Return of the King wins 11 Academy Awards
events.summary: The final Lord of the Rings film sweeps the Oscars.
events.description: On February 29, 2004, The Return of the King, the last film in the adaptation of J.R.R. Tolkien's The Lord of the Rings, received 11 Academy Awards.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: February 29
